source_name: Shiwaforce.com — HU digital delivery partner, bank case studies
why_relevant: Published the Erste Bank Hungary cloud-migration case study, naming the programme and its scope. Local delivery partners' case-study pages are the main way a private bank's transformation team and its size become visible.

source_name: valantic — real-time payment engine case study, Erste Bank Hungary
why_relevant: Vendor case study documenting Erste Bank Hungary's instant-payments hub build. Instant-payment programme vendors are a reliable indirect indicator of payments-org restructuring at HU banks, which never announce such teams themselves.

source_name: ebankIT blog/press — Hungarian bank digital-channel case studies (OTP, Erste)
why_relevant: Carries dedicated pieces on OTP Bank Hungary and Erste Bank Hungary digital transformation. Even where the vendor relationship is marketing-led, the pieces quote named bank executives, which is a usable leadership/org signal for a market with no public procurement trail.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — ATM vendor contract and leadership reporting
why_relevant: The main trade outlet covering Diebold Nixdorf and NCR Atleos bank deals and regional structure changes in Europe. It is the fallback channel for HU ATM-estate outsourcing news, since neither vendor maintains a Hungarian-language newsroom.

source_name: LinkedIn company pages for vendor HU entities (e.g. Nexi Hungary)
why_relevant: For foreign vendors with no Hungarian newsroom, the local LinkedIn page is where a new country lead, a Budapest hub expansion, or a bank-project hiring wave first appears. Highest-signal channel for this cell's leadership-move topic.

source_name: DreamJobs.hu — Hungarian tech employer profiles (e.g. Finshape)
why_relevant: Employer-branding board for HU tech firms. Profiles describe team structure, headcount and the client domains being staffed — a cheap, non-authwalled substitute for LinkedIn when tracking bank-vendor hiring waves.

source_name: MNB személyi engedélyek / ERA — fit-and-proper approvals for financial-sector officers
why_relevant: Where a vendor becomes a licensed payment institution or a bank outsources to a regulated entity, senior-officer appointments require MNB personal approval. This is the only statutory visibility into leadership moves that private banks and their regulated suppliers otherwise keep internal.

source_name: FinTechZone – FinTechShow / BankTechShow speaker rosters (Előadók)
why_relevant: Per-edition speaker pages list name + exact Hungarian job title + institution (e.g. K&H innovation directorate head, CIB IT division head, MBH cloud/automation director, OTP digital growth lead). Archived per edition, so title drift between editions is a direct signal of promotions, role creation and org restructuring at mid/senior level.

source_name: TechShow X (2026 merged FinTechShow + PayTechShow + BankTechShow)
why_relevant: The 2026 jubilee merger of the three FinTechZone shows (14-15 Oct 2026, Várkert Bazár) is the single densest Hungarian gathering of bank/payments titleholders; its agenda will be the largest single-year batch of current titles (MNB Bartha Lajos, Visa regional product director Juhász Katalin already listed).

source_name: Portfolio.hu Rendezvények – conference speaker pages (Előadók / Program)
why_relevant: Portfolio runs the largest recurring Hungarian banking conference series (Hitelezés, Financial IT, Banking Technology, Investment Day, Insurance). Each event has a dedicated /eloadok page with headshot, full Hungarian title and employer — e.g. Nyerges Csilla (ügyvezető igazgató, Large Corporate, Raiffeisen), Bogdán Krisztina (vezérigazgató, ING Bank), Bodor Tibor (vállalati divízió vezetője, K&H). Highest-volume titleholder registry in the cell.

source_name: Portfolio.hu conference preview/recap articles (bank tag)
why_relevant: Pre- and post-event articles name who will speak and in what role, often more current than the static agenda page, and catch last-minute substitutions — a substitution itself frequently signals a departure or reassignment.

source_name: MNB Lámfalussy Lectures Conference – Speakers & Programme
why_relevant: MNB's flagship international conference publishes a structured speaker page plus a 'Previous speakers' archive — an authoritative, dated registry of central-bank and international titles (Governor, MPC member, Chief Economist). Useful for tracking MNB leadership and its counterpart network; the archive gives multi-year title history in one place.

source_name: MNB Conferences hub (Magyar Nemzeti Bank rendezvények)
why_relevant: Index of every MNB-run conference (Lámfalussy Lectures, Budapest Renminbi Initiative, Global Money Week, supervisory conferences). Each child page carries its own speaker list including MNB executive directors (ügyvezető igazgató) and directorate heads — the cheapest window into MNB internal org structure and its churn.

source_name: Mastercard – Év Bankja (Bank of the Year Hungary) official site
why_relevant: The flagship Hungarian banking award, 20th edition in 2025/26, 9 categories across 3 segments (Daily Banking, Innovation, Beyond Banking) with 13 competing institutions. Two registries in one: an archived jury list per year (named journalists, consultants, vendor executives with employers) and winner/shortlist entries that reveal which bank team owns which capability (AI, retention, cybersecurity, merchant partnerships).

source_name: Év Bankja award results coverage – Portfolio / HVG / Pénzcentrum / Világgazdaság / Növekedés / Bank360 / Kreatív
why_relevant: Award-night reporting names the executives who accepted each prize and quotes them with current titles, and 'Az Év Bankára' (Banker of the Year) coverage identifies the individual singled out. This is often the only public place where a specific product/segment owner is attached to a named person.

source_name: FinTechZone – Események (events) category feed
why_relevant: Master index of the Hungarian fintech/banktech event calendar run by the dominant local organiser; leads to every past edition's speaker page and to the 'Best of' flipbooks that photograph and caption speakers with titles.

source_name: Fintech.hu event reporting (Budapest Fintech Week etc.)
why_relevant: Covers the CEE-wide Budapest Fintech Week and panel line-ups, attaching regional fintech and bank leaders to current roles; complements FinTechZone with startup-side and cross-border titles.

source_name: Budapest Fintech Week / Luma event listings
why_relevant: Luma pages for Budapest fintech-week side events publish host and speaker names with employer and role, and often an attendee-count signal; useful for early-stage/startup-side titles that never reach Portfolio agendas.

source_name: Financial Fraud Summit (ffs.ap.hu)
why_relevant: Dedicated Hungarian fraud/payment-security conference whose roster exposes a normally invisible layer: bank security directorates and fraud-prevention leads (e.g. csalásmegelőzés vezető, Bankbiztonsági Igazgatóság). These functions are being built out fast, so new titles here signal new org units.

source_name: BusinessEvents.hu – banking/insurance/investment conference catalogue
why_relevant: Commercial B2B conference organiser with a dedicated bank/insurance/investment vertical (Fraud megelőzés, Pénzmosás megelőzés szaknap, compliance days). Programme pages list named speakers with precise departmental titles from banks and the supervisor — mid-level compliance/AML/fraud roles that no other source enumerates.

source_name: IIR Hungary – financial sector conferences
why_relevant: Long-running paid-conference organiser (Fraud & IT Security, risk, treasury). Archive pages persist for years, giving a historical title series for named bank managers — good for reconstructing career paths and dating role changes retroactively.

source_name: ACFE Hungary Chapter – events
why_relevant: Professional-body chapter whose event and board pages name Hungarian bank fraud-examination and internal-audit officeholders; chapter board composition is itself a small titleholder registry that changes with elections.

source_name: IVSZ (Hungarian ICT Association) event listings
why_relevant: IVSZ co-hosts and lists financial-technology events; its listings often reproduce the speaker line-up and add vendor-side titles (bank technology suppliers), which matters for detecting who a bank's counterpart owner is.

source_name: paytech.events – fintech/banking/payments conference calendar (Hungary entries)
why_relevant: Aggregator that catalogues Hungarian payments events (e.g. TechShow X 2026) with dates, venue and agenda summaries in English — the fastest way to discover event editions we do not yet track, then snowball to the organiser's own speaker page.

source_name: 10times – International Payment Forum / Budapest finance events
why_relevant: Global event directory with Budapest payments-event entries, speaker snippets and exhibitor lists; a cheap discovery layer to catch conferences held in Hungary by foreign organisers that the local press ignores.

source_name: OMFIF Hungary meetings ("Hungary: a regional economic and financial centre")
why_relevant: International think-tank meeting pages give English-language, precisely-worded titles for MNB and Hungarian bank executives — valuable for normalising Hungarian titles to English equivalents and for catching senior appointments announced abroad first.

source_name: Adjacent Budapest business conferences with bank/payments tracks (E-kereskedelmi Konferencia, AI Summit Budapest, Marketing Summit Budapest)
why_relevant: Card-scheme and acquirer staff (e.g. Mastercard üzletfejlesztési igazgató) and bank marketing/digital leaders speak at e-commerce, AI and marketing conferences rather than banking ones. These rosters catch payments commercial roles that banking agendas miss.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – press releases & news (event-linked officeholder mentions)
why_relevant: The banking association names its president, vice-presidents, secretary-general and working-group chairs in event-related releases (its president Jelasity Radován appears as a fixture on conference stages). Association office changes are a leading indicator of member-bank leadership changes.
